book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.name: Whisker Codex
book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.descrip: Start here for practical lessons, placement diagrams and the story of the broken sky.
book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.tooltip: Build, check, and explore the campaign.
book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.categor: Pieces of the old world, caught on your weft. They do not stay.
A safe start, working examples, and what to do when progress stops.
The keepers the Cut snapped. Unlocks as you seat Strands.
What the world was, and what mending it costs. Unlocks as you seat Strands.
What happened, and what still works.
Who kept the Loom. Unlocks as you seat Strands.
book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.entry.b:
**Sigil.** Sixteen Strand Filaments in hand, right-click the Post: **Braid Cord**.\
Then seals and rites — Tribal Power's own, with Nature's Aura, Ars Nouveau, and Occultism as peers. Carve carefully.

**Goal:** spin **Braid Cord** and seat Sigil.\
You need **16 Strand Filaments** and a **Tension Post**.\
**Check:** Right-click the Post holding 16 Strand Filaments for **Braid Cord**. Finish Sigil, then seat the Sigil token.

Read **Start here** for worked examples. Recipes live in JEI; the **Spirit Codex** covers Tribal Power machinery. If you get stuck, test one recipe at a time and sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent machine.
**Swarm.** There are no bees to find in the void, so you make somewhere a bee wants to be: a ring of oak logs around a small flower, placed on the pad. Wait. Wings.

Every nest is the same trick with a different ring — gravel, coarse dirt, stone, quartz, end stone. Then hives, a centrifuge, an incubator, and deep essence crops. Keep something alive that keeps something else alive.

**Goal:** finish Swarm and seat the Swarm token.\
You need a nest the pad can actually grow — oak logs around a flower — then hives.\
**Check:** Finish Swarm. Claim the token and seat it. The Swarm notch lights.

Read **Start here** for worked examples. Recipes live in JEI; the **Spirit Codex** covers Tribal Power machinery. If you get stuck, test one recipe at a time and sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent machine.

**Claw.** Silent Gear plans, iron on your back, a bow, a portal frame. Leave the pad on purpose.\
Claiming a pad wipes Silent Gear's join gift. Four **Blueprint Paper**, shapeless, make a **Blueprint Package**. Right-click to unwrap starter plans.\
Edge opens the braid: after Claw, Pattern, Colony, and Hum are all yours to choose from.

**Goal:** finish Claw and seat the Claw token.\
You need four **Blueprint Paper** if the join gift is gone, then iron on your back.\
**Check:** Finish Claw. If the Blueprint Package is missing, craft it from four Blueprint Paper, then seat the Claw token. The Claw notch lights.

Read **Start here** for worked examples. Recipes live in JEI; the **Spirit Codex** covers Tribal Power machinery. If you get stuck, test one recipe at a time and sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent machine.

**Spark.** Strike a Drumheart before you touch a wire. Spirit Pulse is the power fantasy here; Powah and Mekanism are bridges you cross later, if you want.\
Bone Chime, Spirit Shard, Copper Resonator, Drumheart. Then listen.

**Goal:** finish Spark and seat the Spark token.\
You need a **Drumheart** and the first Pulse trickle from Start here.\
**Check:** Finish Spark. Claim the token and seat it. The Spark notch lights.

Read **Start here** for worked examples. Recipes live in JEI; the **Spirit Codex** covers Tribal Power machinery. If you get stuck, test one recipe at a time and sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent machine.

**Goal:** run one rite and one travel tool the Spirit Codex already diagrams.\
You need the **Spirit Codex**; those shapes live there, not here.\
Stone Font, Listening Pit, Rite Circle, Voice Ring, Shatter Array, Way Gate and Far Gate are Spirit Codex shapes. Whisker does not reprint them.

The Gate Drum is the portable way into the March. Charge it with Pulse, then empty-handed use it. Do not strike it like a Drumheart.\
Bind a return compass before you go. `/tribalpower gate list` names later gates.
**Check:** one Font or Pit from the Spirit Codex diagram produces an output. If it stays silent, crouch and right-click with the Spirit Codex.

Tribal Weave is the workshop beside the nine Strands. Rhythm, landscape and reusable Echo catalysts make Pulse.\
Open the **Spirit Codex** for every generator, station, relay, Kiln, Voice Ring and rite. Sneak-use it on a silent machine. This book does not copy those manuals.

**Goal:** a Resonator that can feed Spark, then the later workshops the Spirit Codex diagrams.\
You need the **Spirit Codex** and a working Pulse Resonator from Start here.\
1\. Finish **Make the first Echo Shard** and **Start automatic power** in Start here.\
2\. Keep the Spirit Codex on your hotbar while you run Tribal Weave.
3\. Slot faces, Shatter-on-Kiln, relays, compass landings and the sixth Loom voice live in that book, not here.
**Check:** sneak-use the Spirit Codex on the Resonator. Stored Pulse should rise with two different voices and a catalyst seated.

**Clock.** Create. Water wheels, presses, mixers, belts — one cog, then the same cog again.\
The precision mechanism wants a Binding Knot at its heart. That is the Loom asking to be included.

**Goal:** finish Clock and seat the Clock token.\
You need Create started and a Binding Knot for the precision mechanism.\
**Check:** Finish Clock. Claim the token and seat it. The Clock notch lights.

Read **Start here** for worked examples. Recipes live in JEI; the **Spirit Codex** covers Tribal Power machinery. If you get stuck, test one recipe at a time and sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent machine.

**Stone.** Unravel Thread to string, spin yarn, tie a Knot, raise a Loomframe. The Tension Barrel makes clay; clay makes porcelain; porcelain carries lava.\
Then the sieve. It is a tool inside Recover, not the name of it. Iron mesh is the target: that is where Strand Filament starts falling.

**Goal:** finish Recover and seat the Stone token.\
You need Frayed Thread, a **Loomframe**, a **Tension Barrel**, and a mesh.\
**Check:** Finish Recover. Claim the Stone token and seat it. The Stone notch lights. A working Loomframe and Tension Barrel are the practical check.

Read **Start here** for worked examples. Recipes live in JEI; the **Spirit Codex** covers Tribal Power machinery. If you get stuck, test one recipe at a time and sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent machine.

**Spindle.** A digital loom (AE2, with a Knot in the controller and a Braid in the assembler). A Gate Drum. The March, and a March stone from it.\
Nine seated, one stone, one right-click: the Fragment. Seat it. The cut closes above your pad.

**Goal:** close your Clowder's cut with March Stone.\
You need nine seated tokens and **March Stone** from the March.\
**Check:** Seat all nine tokens. Right-click the Post with March Stone for a **Spindle Loom Fragment**, then right-click again holding the Fragment. Your Clowder's Strand of the Fray closes.

Read **Start here** for worked examples. Recipes live in JEI; the **Spirit Codex** covers Tribal Power machinery. If you get stuck, test one recipe at a time and sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent machine.

**Sprout.** A wheat field, a kitchen, then Mystical Agriculture. Sieve dirt for Inferium Ore and gravel for Prosperity Ore — smelt them, and the essence-seed tiers open up. Botany pots if you like compact.\
Food is infrastructure here. A Clowder that eats well leaves the pad sooner.

**Goal:** finish Sprout and keep food running.\
You need a kitchen source and the Sprout token from the chapter.\
**Check:** Finish Sprout. Claim the token and seat it. The Sprout notch lights. Keep a food source running before you leave the pad.

Read **Start here** for worked examples. Recipes live in JEI; the **Spirit Codex** covers Tribal Power machinery. If you get stuck, test one recipe at a time and sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent machine.

**Soil.** Wood, dirt, a bench, a sapling, a chest, warmth. Melt ice with lava for water on Normal and Hard. Cook something.\
The Soil token comes from the **Soil Knot** at the end of the chapter. Raise a Tension Post and seat it. The pad starts mending you.

**Goal:** finish Soil and seat the Soil token.\
You need the **Soil Knot** claimed and a **Tension Post** placed.\
**Check:** Finish Soil in the quest screen. Claim the **Soil Knot**, then seat the Soil token. The Soil notch lights.

Read **Start here** for worked examples. Recipes live in JEI; the **Spirit Codex** covers Tribal Power machinery. If you get stuck, test one recipe at a time and sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent machine.
book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.entry.d: How a wreck arrives, and how to reach it.

**Goal:** reach a Driftwreck before it unravels.\
Once your Clowder has tensioned Soil, pieces of the old world drift up to your pad now and then: roughly once every hour and a half of play, or sooner if you hang a **Driftlure** on your Tension Post.

The Steward tells the whole Clowder when one is caught, and the **Drift Needle** points at it.\
Stand at your pad's edge, face the wreck and use a **Tether Spool**: a thread bridge lays itself across.

A wreck only ages while someone in your Clowder is online.\
It creaks at half its time, starts to crumble at the rim near the end, and then unravels.

Nobody falls: anyone on it is lifted home, and whatever you left in its chests comes home in a **Salvage Bundle** (in your **Salvage Crate**, if one stands by the Post).\
Fall off the tether and the thread catches you, for three hearts.
Every wreck asks one thing: open its heart chest, break its frayed spawners, light its thread pillars in the order the idol shows, walk a lost Steward echo home, or hold the seam through three waves.

Do it and each of you gets **Salvaged Weft** and a **Seal**, the **Wreck Atlas** fills a page, and sometimes a **Keepsake** comes home.\
**Check:** your Atlas shows the new page.
Spend Weft on spools, lures, needles, map scrolls, Weft Keys, tribe decor and reprints of Keepsakes you already found.

The Claw Smithy made crampons, hooks and pitons, and tested every one by hanging the smith from it over the void. A smith who trusted their work was a smith who lived. Their hooks still hold. The walls around them do not.

Edge-walkers kept gardens on ledges no one else could reach: cliff-roses, rope-moss, a stubborn kind of bean. A ledge bed was a reward for a new route. Some of these beds are still blooming on a piece of cliff that is no longer attached to anything. Climb.

Edge-walkers wrote their routes as knotted cords, one knot for every safe foothold, so they could read them in the dark. The Route Loft held thousands. The longest cord led to an island nobody else believed in. The cord ends past the edge.

Edge-walkers left a claw mark on the Last Post Shrine each time they returned from past the fence. Old walkers had stones covered in marks. Young ones had one, and were loud about it. The newest mark on this stone is unfinished.

At the end of their longest route the Edge-walkers built the Far Cache: rope, food, a bed, a note for the next walker. Whoever reached it wore the gold clasp home. The clasp never made it home the last time. It is going home now.

The Brink Watch hung over nothing, braced on three iron claws driven into the cliff. Edge-walkers stood there to learn the wind before they stepped off. You were not an Edge-walker until you had eaten a meal at the Brink with your feet dangling. Sit.

In the Gear Loft Pattern-weavers cut cogs by hand and matched them by ear. A good pair of gears hummed a single note. This cog belonged to a machine that fed a whole island. One cog, then the same cog again.
Pattern-weavers grew a garden that repeated: a hedge maze whose paths were a round sung in green. Walk it right and you came out singing. Walk it wrong and you came out where you began. Try again.

The Pattern Stacks held every loop the Pattern-weavers ever sang into a machine. Their machines ran on patterns the way others ran on fire. The last loop in the stacks was never finished. It keeps trying to repeat.

Pattern-weavers sang in rounds: one voice began, the next followed, until a hall of voices turned like gears. The Round Chapel was built so the echo arrived exactly one beat late. The echo is still arriving. Nobody started it.

The Pattern-weavers' vault opened once a year, at a minute only the Hour Tower could count. The minute came and went during the Cut with no one at the door. The box is still waiting for its hour. Wind it.

The Hour Tower rang every hour for every island, so nine tribes could keep one time. Pattern-weavers adjusted it with a key the size of an arm. After the Cut the islands drifted apart and the hours stopped matching. The tower rings anyway.
The heart of the old world

Before the Cut the nine tribes met in one hall at the centre of the old world, each district facing the loom in the middle.\
They were not one people and never tried to be.\
They were one weave.\
The Skies were never an ending.

They were the Loom, holding its breath while you learned to hold the thread.\
Go on weaving.
A loose page about hidden rooms.

The forge-keepers kept their best work where the hammer fell.\
*From now on, your Clowder's forge wrecks drift in with their hidden room open.*
A loose page about hidden rooms.

The gardeners buried what they loved under the water they gave it.\
*From now on, your Clowder's garden wrecks drift in with their hidden room open.*
A loose page about hidden rooms.

One shelf in every library was never meant to be read.\
*From now on, your Clowder's library wrecks drift in with their hidden room open.*
A loose page about hidden rooms.

The shrine-tenders kept the best offering under the stone they knelt on.\
*From now on, your Clowder's shrine wrecks drift in with their hidden room open.*
A loose page about hidden rooms.

A vault with one wall is a door. A vault with two is a promise.\
*From now on, your Clowder's vault wrecks drift in with their hidden room open.*
A loose page about hidden rooms.

Three landings up, the watch kept a room nobody climbed to.\
*From now on, your Clowder's watchtower wrecks drift in with their hidden room open.*

At the Carving Bench a Seal-carver could press spirit into matter and make it stay. Their tools wore down to fit the hand of one carver and no other. When a carver died, their burin was buried with their last seal. This one was not buried.

Seal-carvers grew amethyst the way others grew herbs, in beds of calcite watered with salt. Each crystal took a lifetime and a seal pressed into it at the start. The beds are still growing. The seals are still working.

The Rune Library held a rubbing of every seal ever carved, so a broken seal could be carved again. Seal-carvers read by candlelight, tracing runes with a finger. This is a rubbing of their first seal. Nobody alive can carve it.

Seal-carvers made promises in stone: a sigil carved at the Oath Stone bound whoever carved it. The stone was covered edge to edge with oaths kept and broken. One oath at the centre is still glowing. It is still being kept.

Under the Oath Stone the Seal-carvers built a vault closed with nine seals and no door. What it holds is a question for a braver Clowder. A seal is a promise the world has to keep. This one is still kept.

The Ward Beacon lit a ring of wards around the Seal-carvers' island every night. Nothing walked through the light that was not invited. The night of the Cut the ring held. It was the island underneath that broke. Carve carefully.

The Pad-keepers forged nothing sharper than a mattock and needed nothing sharper. They re-edged the same heads for generations, so a tool outlived three owners. The shed smelled of wet iron and bread. Bank the fire before you leave.

The Warm Bed was a garden built over the Hearthbank's ash pit, so it never froze. Pad-keepers grew their first shoots there and carried them out to the cold fields in clay jars. It fed everyone. It could not feed a pad that was drifting.

The Seedlist House kept one page for every seed the Pad-keepers ever planted, with who planted it and what it gave back. Children learned to read from the harvest columns. Half the pages are still blank. They were saving room.

The Pad-keepers rang a root-bell at dusk so the soil would hold its warmth through the night. Every family carried a handful of hearth-ash to the Hearthbank. When the Cut came the bell was still warm, and someone kept ringing it.

Under the Warm Bed the Pad-keepers dug a cellar and filled it with one of every seed, sealed in tin, against a bad year. The bad year was worse than they planned for. The tins are still full. Plant them.

From the Long Furrow Post a Pad-keeper could see every field at once and tell which one was thirsty by its colour. They signalled with lanterns: green for rain, red for frost. The last lantern hung red for a week before the post let go.
In the Spark Forge the bellows worked in time with a drum, so the fire rose and fell like breath. Drumhearts said iron forged off the beat would crack. Their tools are still whole. Keep time.

The Ember Gardens grew around the forge's warm run-off: fire-peppers, sunroot, a flower that bloomed only at a hard beat. Drumhearts ate spicy and played loud. The run-off is cold now. The peppers are still hot.

The Measure House kept every rhythm the Drumhearts ever played, scratched into copper plates. A child could learn the whole history of the tribe by drumming it. The last plate is only four beats long. Someone was in a hurry.

Drumhearts believed the sky had a heartbeat and that someone had to keep time with it. At the Pulse Circle a drummer played every hour of every day for three hundred years. The beat stopped during the Cut. Then, faintly, it started again.
The Charge Vault stored the Thunder Mast's catch in sealed coils for the long, still winters. One coil could keep a hall warm for a season. This one was never opened. Listen before you open it.

The Thunder Mast caught lightning and stored it in copper coils for the drums below. Drumhearts climbed it in storms to listen to the coils hum. When the Cut opened, the mast caught something that was not lightning. The horn blew three short notes.

At the Shuttle Works the Loom-stitchers carved shuttles that could carry thread through the sky itself. Each one crossed the void a thousand times before it wore out. This one did not wear out. It was dropped.

The Loom-stitchers grew their own thread: a blue flax field on a slope above the looms, harvested by every hand on the island at once. It was the only day the looms were quiet. The field still flowers blue. Harvest it.

The Thread Archive kept the pattern of the old sky on punched cards: every island, every path, every knot between them. The Loom-stitchers could weave it again if they had to. They had to. The cards are nearly all still here.

The Loom-stitchers' chapel held a small loom that was never stopped: whoever passed added a thread. It was a weaving of everyone who ever visited. When they cut the gate-paths, they meant to come back and finish it. It is still unfinished.

In the Gate Vault the Loom-stitchers kept the one tapestry they never showed: all nine tribes woven together, with a thread left loose at the edge on purpose. They always meant to come back. Stitch the cut. Then go and see what the March kept for you.

From the Gate Lookout the Loom-stitchers watched the gate-paths they had cut through the sky, and mended them when they frayed. Every stitch in the sky was theirs. The day of the Cut they saw the whole weave tear at once. They ran to fix it.

Rootbinders did not forge metal; they grafted. In the Grafting Shed a patient hand could join an apple to a thorn and make it fruit. Their best work was a bridge of two trees grown together across a gap. Half of it fell when the island did.

The Nursery Terraces fed three islands from one slope, watered by roots that pulled mist out of the clouds. Rootbinders sang to the seedlings, mostly to keep themselves awake. Something in the soil still sprouts at dawn. Feed it.

In the Leaf Archive, Rootbinders pressed one leaf from every plant they tended, with the date it first bloomed. Reading the pages in order is like watching a spring arrive. The last page holds a leaf nobody could name. It arrived with the Cut.

Rootbinders tied a living knot into a sapling for every child and planted it at the Anchor Grove. The trees grew roots deep enough to hold the island still in a gale. Where the Cut ran, the roots held on to both halves. They are holding still.

The Rootbinders' vault was a hollow grown inside one ancient trunk, sealed by bark as it healed. What they kept there was not treasure but cuttings of every tree, alive and asleep. The trunk is still healing around them. Wake one.

The Canopy Lookout was never built: the Rootbinders grew it, coaxing a trunk into a stair over forty summers. From the top you could watch weather roll across nine islands. The trunk kept growing after the watchers left. It is taller now.

The Grit Mill ground stone to sand by song: the millstones turned faster when the singers held a high note. A good miller could grade grit by ear alone. The mill still turns when the wind is right. Nobody grades the grit now.

Grit-singers grew lichen on their terraces the way others grew flowers, and read the seasons in its rings. A lichen stone was a gift for a newborn. Some of these rings are older than the Cut. Keep counting.
The Echo Register was a wall of carved staves, one for every quarry, marking the pitch of its best stone. Masons came from nine valleys to read it. Where a stave is chipped, the quarry is gone.

Grit-singers named every shard by the note it gave when struck, and the Hall of Echoes was where the names were sung aloud. A choir of forty could make the whole cliff hum. After the Cut the hall kept humming with nobody in it.

The Hollow Vault had no keyhole: its door opened to a single sustained note that only its keepers knew. When the keepers scattered, the note scattered with them. This key hums the first half of it. Find the rest.

The Listening Spire leaned into the wind so its stones would ring when a rockfall began far off. Grit-singers took turns sleeping at the top with their ear to the wall. The last watcher heard the Cut coming. There was no note for it.

At the Wax Works, Colony-keepers cast candles, sealed jars and poured the wax that held their houses together. Nothing they built had a nail in it. Warm hands kept it all standing. It stood for longer than anyone expected.

The Bloom Fields were planted for bees, not people: row on row of flowers timed so something was always open. Colony-keepers ate what the bees left. The fields still bloom on schedule. Keep something alive that keeps something else alive.

The Comb Archive kept the tribe's accounts on wax tablets, stacked like honeycomb: every hive, every harvest, every jar given away. Colony-keepers gave away more than they kept. The last tablet is a list of names. They are all marked as fed.

Colony-keepers built their altar inside a hive and prayed by humming in the same key as the bees. The whole island buzzed on feast days. When the Cut came, the bees went quiet first. Then they hummed louder than they ever had.
Deep in the comb the Colony-keepers kept a vault for the next queen: royal jelly, the warmest wax, a cell nobody else could enter. She had not hatched when the Cut came. The cell is still warm. Wait.

From the Drone Tower the Colony-keepers read the swarms like weather: which way they flew, how high, how loud. A low swarm meant rain. On the day of the Cut every swarm on the island flew straight up. Look up.
book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.entry.f: Start automatic power
Practical steps and checks.
Goal

**Goal:** a Pulse Resonator that makes a small, steady trickle of Pulse without you standing at the drum.\
You need a **Pulse Resonator**, an **Echo Shard**, and **Earth and Fire Resonance Totems**.
Starter generator

1\. Place the Resonator.\
2\. Right-click it with the shard to install the reusable catalyst.\
3\. Place the two different totems within 8 blocks. The diagram shows a compact example.\
4\. Wait a second and inspect the generator. Stored Pulse should rise.
Power budget

**Check:** stored Pulse climbs while you stand still.\
The starter generator does not mean every machine can run continuously. If a machine spends power faster than you make it, let a reserve build up or improve generation.
Two identical totems count as one element. If generation stops, check the catalyst, different elements and pausing redstone. Read the Spirit Codex before larger totem layouts or a Conductor.

book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.entry.f: Choose two middle branches
Practical steps and checks.
Three routes

**Goal:** spin **Braid Cord** at the Post, then work the three middle branches.\
You need **16 Strand Filaments** and a **Tension Post**. No Strand has to be seated first.\
After Claw, three branches open together:\
**Pattern / Clock:** mechanical processing.

**Colony / Swarm:** bees and their production chains.\
**Hum / Spark:** living power and workshops.\
A team can divide the work. You will still need all nine Strands for the final reweave.
Make Braid Cord

1\. Stand at your **Tension Post**.\
2\. Hold **16 Strand Filaments** — sieve gravel or sand with an iron Thread Mesh.\
3\. Right-click the Post to receive **Braid Cord**.
Do not put Strand tokens in a crafting grid. They record progress, and the braid does not need them.
Check
**Check:** two of those three notches are lit, and Braid Cord is in your hand. Next: Bind and the Sigil quests.
Claw Blueprint Package
Practical steps and checks.
Goal

**Goal:** get Silent Gear starter plans when Claw opens, even if the join gift is gone.\
You need four **Blueprint Paper**.\
Claiming a pad wipes Silent Gear's first-join **Blueprint Package**. That is Skyblock Builder clearing the inventory, not a missing recipe.
Craft the package

1\. Reach the Claw / Edge quests. Open a Blueprint Paper in JEI if you need the current paper recipe.\
2\. Craft a **Blueprint Package** from four **Blueprint Paper**, shapeless.\
3\. Right-click the package to unwrap starter plans.
4\. Follow Claw for rods, tools, iron on your back, a bow, and a portal frame. Leave the pad on purpose.
Check

**Check:** you are holding the package or the unwrapped plans, and the Claw quest can see them.\
Do not wait for another join gift. Tokens still are not crafted in a grid. After Claw, Pattern, Colony and Hum open together.
Prepare the final reweave
Practical steps and checks.
Readiness checklist

**Goal:** seat all nine Strands, bring March Stone home, and close your Clowder's cut.\
You need nine seated tokens, **March Stone**, and a way home.\
Count the Post notches before you leave. Prepare food, equipment and a return route. The **Spirit Codex** covers the Gate Drum and March travel.
Use the Post twice

1\. With all nine Strands seated, right-click the Tension Post with March Stone. This makes a **Spindle Loom Fragment**.\
2\. Right-click the Post again, this time holding the Fragment, to reweave your team's sky.\
These are world interactions, not crafting-table recipes.
Check
**Check:** nine notches are lit, then the Fragment seats and the Fray over the Dock is thinner for your Clowder. If nothing happens, read the Post message. Other teams have their own progress.
Make the first Echo Shard
Practical steps and checks.
Goal and supplies

**Goal:** make an Echo Shard for an automatic generator.\
You need Echo Shatter, an Earth Resonance Totem, a Drumheart and **stone**, not cobblestone. Smelt cobblestone if necessary.\
Use the **Spirit Codex** for Tribal Power recipes, diagrams and troubleshooting. Sneak-use it on the station if it stays silent.
Build and run it

1\. Place the drum and Earth totem beside Echo Shatter, within 8 blocks.\
2\. Right-click the drum with an empty hand about once a second. Build a reserve of Pulse.\
3\. Put stone into Shatter and leave output space.

4\. Wait for an Echo Shard. If it stops, charge the drum again and inspect the station with the Spirit Codex.\
Cobblestone becomes gravel instead. A slow generator can finish a batch using stored energy.
Check
**Check:** an Echo Shard is in the output. The diagram is a compact example, not a quest shape.
Finish and seat Soil
Practical steps and checks.
Goal

**Goal:** finish Soil and seat its token so the pad starts mending you.\
You need the Soil Knot claimed and a **Tension Post** placed.\
Completing a quest and seating its token are separate steps.
Complete the chapter

1\. Open the quest screen and work through Soil. Read each task: some need you to hold an item; others ask you to craft or perform an action. Click the item to open JEI if the recipe is unclear.\
2\. Claim the **Soil Knot** reward when its tasks are complete.

3\. Craft and place a **Tension Post** using its current recipe.\
4\. Right-click the Post with the Soil Strand token.
Check the Post

**Check:** the Soil notch lights and your team gains the seated Strand.\
If the notch stays dark, check that you claimed the token and are holding the right item. Team progress is shared; you do not need a separate Post for every player.\
Next: Recover introduces the Loomframe, barrel and material processing.
Hold liquids safely
Practical steps and checks.
Goal

**Goal:** store and move liquids without dumping them on the floor.\
You need a **Spirit Cistern** (JEI / Tribal Weave). AE2 Sky Stone Tanks empty when broken.\
AE2 **Sky Stone Tanks** empty when broken. That is AE2's design, not a pack bug. Bucket them out before you pick the tank up.
Use a Cistern

1\. Craft a **Spirit Cistern**. It holds 16 buckets of one fluid.\
2\. Fill it with a bucket or a standard fluid pipe. A comparator reads fullness; redstone can lock filling and draining.\
3\. Break the Cistern when you need to move it. The fluid stays on the dropped block.

4\. Relays move fluid between loaded ends. They are paths, not tanks.\
The **Spirit Codex** has the current piping and Wave Drum details. The diagram is one compact corner, not a quest shape.
Check
**Check:** put a bucket into the Cistern, pick the block up, and place it again. The fluid is still there. If you used a Sky Stone Tank, the liquid is gone unless you bucketed first.
Build a material supply
Practical steps and checks.
Goal and sequence

**Goal:** turn pad scraps into materials for Recover and the chapters after it.\
You need Frayed Thread, Recover open, and a mesh.\
1\. Unravel Frayed Thread into string when you need it. Keep some Thread for trading.\
2\. Follow JEI for Void Yarn, a Binding Knot and a Loomframe.

3\. Make a Tension Barrel and keep water nearby.\
4\. Follow Recover for clay, porcelain and the route to handling lava.
Test small batches
Read the Loomframe and barrel in JEI before adding items. Start with one batch and check the output. Keep the input and result in separate storage until you know the process.
**Check:** the Loomframe produces scraps from a loaded mesh, and the barrel returns clay or yarn. Adjacent placement alone does not automate these stations. The next model is a workspace example.
Sieves

**Goal:** a click sieve for early grit, then a hopper Loomframe.\
You need an oak sieve, a string mesh, and cobble to hammer.\
1\. Craft an **oak sieve**. Hold a mesh and right-click the sieve; this one is hand-only.

2\. Hammer cobble toward gravel, sand or dust as Recover asks. String mesh first; iron mesh is when **Strand Filament** starts.\
3\. The **Loomframe** is the hopper machine: mesh by hand, dirt/gravel/sand/dust in the top, output below.

**Check:** the oak sieve yields a click of grit, and the Loomframe ticks with a loaded mesh. Follow Recover and JEI for the current mesh and substrate. Adjacent placement does not automate either station.
Pad-runners
Practical steps and checks.
Goal

**Goal:** find a wild pad-runner in the March, not on your void pad.\
You need a charged **Gate Drum**, **Gysahl**, and **Sage Notes**.\
Birds do not spawn on a skyblock island. There is no spawn-egg shortcut and no join gift. Walk the March.
Find, tame, ride

1\. Charge a **Gate Drum** with Pulse, then empty-handed use it and walk through. Do not strike it like a Drumheart. Yellows graze the Steppe and Reed Fen. Snow Fields hide Wonderful grades. Ember Wastes keep Flame birds.

2\. Pick **Gysahl** in the March (Reed Fen is densest). Craft extras into seeds and plant them on dirt or March soil at home.\
3\. Craft **Sage Notes** (book and a gysahl leaf) and right-click a bird to read it.
4\. Tame a wild yellow with gysahl, then saddle it. Sprint dashes; ease off to recover stamina.
Esther at the hub

After you have walked the March, **Esther** stands at Clowder Hall (`/clowder hub`). Mount a saddled bird and speak to her, or place a **Square Gate**.\
**Check:** you are on a saddled bird, or Esther is waiting at the hub.
Farm and colour

**Goal:** train, mate, and paint colours without chasing dyes that do not exist.\
You need greens to train, nuts to mate, and **Sage Notes** to read the bird.\
1\. Train an adult on greens until it is sated on each kind. Krakka is two gysahl and bone meal.

2\. Mate with nuts. Talent follows the nut. Colour follows the parents unless Carob or Zeio is involved.\
3\. **Carob** (ravagers): two Good-or-better Yellows hatch Green or Blue. Each parent needs 1 first-place race; 4 combined firsts make the colour certain.
4\. Green plus Blue hatch Black (a miss is White) — 2 firsts each, 9 combined for a sure roll. **Zeio** (piglin brutes): Black plus a Wonderful Yellow hatch Gold — 3 firsts each, 12 combined.

5\. There are no Pink or Red birds. The Fair stall does not sell those dyes. Purple is End; Flame is Ember Wastes; Gold flies.\
**Check:** Sage Notes shows colour, grade, class, race wins and the last nut. Recipes stay in JEI.
Your first safe workshop
Practical steps and checks.
Goal and supplies

**Goal:** a safe place to grow a tree, craft, store items and cook food.\
You need a sapling, dirt, and the starter supplies.\
Keep a sapling, some dirt and the starter supplies. Open the Soil quests before spending rare starter items.
Clowder and Hall

**Goal:** one Clowder, one pad, a way back to the Hall.\
You need the **Island Charter** and a **Hub Key**.\
1\. **K** opens the island/team panel. The **Island Charter** opens the same panel. Join or create a team, then pick a pad.

2\. Hold the Charter and right-click a friend to invite, or `/clowder invite <name>` / `/clowder accept`.\
3\. Sneak-use the Charter on solid Overworld pad ground to seal spawn.\
4\. **Hub Key** or `/clowder hub` reaches Clowder Hall. `/clowder return` sends you home. Right-click a Hall Elder to trade Frayed Thread.
**Check:** you are on your pad, in the intended Clowder, and `/clowder hub` works.
Build in this order

1\. Widen your platform. Add edges and light.\
2\. Harvest wood. Keep a replacement sapling and replant it on dirt.\
3\. Make a crafting table and chest. Store spare saplings and valuables.\
4\. Make a furnace. Cook food as the Soil quests request. Keep walkways clear.
Workshop check

**Check:** a replanted tree, spare materials in storage, cooked food, and a workspace you can walk around without falling.\
The model on the next page is one compact arrangement. Build a larger platform around it. The exact arrangement is optional. Keep fire and lava away from wooden floors.
When progress stops
Practical steps and checks.
Quest checks

**Goal:** unstick one blocked task without rebuilding the pad.\
You need the quest screen, JEI, and (for Tribal) the **Spirit Codex**.

Read the exact task and its prerequisites. Check item counts, variants and whether the task wants possession, crafting or another action. Click the quest item to open JEI. Try the task's detect button when one is available.

Check rewards too: an unclaimed token cannot be seated. If Claw is stuck on plans, craft the Blueprint Package from four Blueprint Paper. If playing together, confirm you are in the intended Clowder before repeating a long crafting chain.
Machine checks

Check these separately:\
1\. Correct input and recipe.\
2\. Available power and range.\
3\. Required totem or other structure.

4\. Space for the result.\
5\. Pausing redstone and side settings.\
For Tribal Power, crouch and right-click the machine with the Spirit Codex. Test one machine before connecting a whole production line.
Shared lives

When shared lives are on (default), each Clowder mate adds **three** lives to one team pool. A survival death spends one. Food and potions do not put it back. At zero, affected players become spectators.
`/skybound lives` prints the pool. Six quest rewards named **Thread of Return** each add one life when claimed, once per Clowder.

After those, a **Thread of Return** is an item: four **Thread Shards** stitched around a Braid Cord, right-clicked for one more shared life, as often as you can pay for it. Cut a Shard from diamonds, Void Yarn and a Rift Shard, or buy one from Spark at `/clowder hub`.
Keep one in a pocket **before** the pool empties: at zero you are already a spectator and cannot use anything. Operators run `/skybound revive`. Plan trips together.
Common traps

A Sky Stone Tank that you just moved is empty unless you bucketed first. Use a Spirit Cistern to carry liquids.\
Pad-runners are in the March, not on the pad. After the Gate, Esther waits at `/clowder hub`.\
**Check:** you have isolated one cause from this page, not rebuilt the whole workshop on a guess.
Using the Codex
Practical steps and checks.
Book and quests

**Goal:** know which screen does which job before you build anything.\
You need the **Whisker Codex** from the starter kit or dock chest.

Use the **Whisker Codex** to learn a system, then build it. Open the quest screen with the **Grave / backtick** key for tasks, requirements and rewards. If you changed controls, search Controls for Quests.
Click a quest item to open its recipe in JEI. Start with **Start here**. **The Loom Braid** is the campaign map. Story chapters wait until you want the why.
Read, build, check

Each practical lesson gives a goal, numbered steps and a way to check the result. Follow the arrows.\
Exact ingredients live in JEI, not in this book. Recipes can change with the pack. A diagram is a placement example, not a quest requirement.

**Tribal Power** is its own mod. Open its **Spirit Codex** for every generator, workshop, rite and camp hand. This book is the pack campaign: pad, quests, Loom, Clowder. Sneak-use the Spirit Codex on a silent Tribal station.
Words in this book

**Pad:** your floating island.\
**Clowder:** your player team.\
**Strand:** one part of the campaign.\
**Token:** the reward proving you completed a Strand.

**Seat:** right-click a Tension Post with a token.\
**Pulse:** the energy used by Tribal Power.\
**March:** the otherworld beyond the Gate Drum.\
**Check:** Grave opens quests. A quest item opens JEI. **Start here** is the first category in this book.
Keep a water supply
Practical steps and checks.
Goal and supplies

**Goal:** a refillable water source that will not burn the pad.\
You need ice, lava and an empty bucket on Normal/Hard. Easy pads already have water.\
Easy pads include water. Normal and Hard pads supply ice, lava and an empty bucket.
First water source

1\. Make a contained area from nonflammable blocks.\
2\. Put the ice where the water should remain. Use nearby lava as the heat source, with blocks containing its flow.\
3\. Let the ice melt. Collect the resulting water source with the bucket.
Keep lava away from wood and stored items. Do not let the two liquids flow together.
A refillable pool
**Once you have two water source buckets**, build the four-block pool shown next. Fill opposite corners. On ordinary water-source rules, all four spaces become sources.
**Check:** collect a bucket and watch the pool refill before you rely on it. One source alone is not enough for this layout. Keep water available for the Tension Barrel and farming.

A shape the Cut left on the shard, not a confession of who swung.\

The Hivemind is fragile but every wave its six cells pour drones. A campfire set on a drone cell seals it for thirty seconds; seal all six and the royal chamber opens for ten. Your own Productive Bees attack the drones on sight.\

Your own restored Loom turned against you. The Overweaver throws shades of the nine guardians onto their strands; kill a shade and its thread pulls taut for twenty-five seconds, and only then can the loom itself be hurt. Later it throws three, then all nine.
**Check:** `/guardians status` lists this win, and you hold the Woven Relic.

Dispel the pillars in that order with an Ars dispel or any Sigil-strand item; a wrong one re-arms all three and the ward-glass bites.\
Three right and it is open for twelve seconds.

book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.entry.m: Named continents
Pads that forgot they were pads. Cities that hung. Hearths first.
Named continents

The old maps did not say *island*.\
They named continents the way you name a house: by who kept the hearth, by which river had manners, by which city hung over which Strand-knot.\
A pad that had forgotten it was a pad got a name.
A name was a promise that the inspection had gone well for long enough to stop calling it a pad.
Cities that hung

Markets sat on lattice, not bedrock. Stairs went down to the under-thread and up to the weather-road. You could walk a street and never think about the drop because the Soil Strand ran under the cobbles the way warmth runs under a well-kept floor.
Hanging felt like standing. That was the trick, and it was work.
Hearths first

Before Stone named shards, before Clock sang a factory, a Pad-keeper banked heat in thin dirt and called it a world. The hearth is the first physics. A continent is a hearth that got out of hand in the useful direction.
Seat Soil and you are not founding a nation. You are reminding a scrap of dirt that it used to be allowed to stay warm.
The first cold
The hearths went out while the sky still looked whole.
The first cold

The Pad-keepers kept the warmth, not the fires — banked heat in thin dirt that let a family sleep through a long dark. They felt the Cut before anyone named it. Pads got cold. Bread took longer to rise. Moss would not take.
They carried dirt in baskets, a pad at a time, and set a hearth on every scrap they saved. That is why you have a pad at all.
What Soil remembers

Seat Soil and the pad starts mending you. That is not a blessing invented for Skybound. It is the old hearth-trick, scaled down to whatever dirt is left. The Strand still knows how to keep a body warm if you ask it in the old way: a token, a Post, a promise kept.
On good terms
You do not own a hive. You are on good terms with it.
On good terms

The Colony-keepers tended hives that hummed in the Loom's own key, and March flowers that hummed back. They did not own their colonies. They were on good terms with them. When the sky fell, a great many hives went quiet rather than angry. Quiet is a kind of loyalty.
There are no bees to find in the void. You make somewhere a bee wants to be, and you wait.
What Swarm mends

Seat Swarm and you are resuming a conversation, not founding a livestock industry. Keep something alive that keeps something else alive. Take without asking and the comb goes quiet. It is very patient about this.
A sky that was a floor
Before anything fell.
Hanging continents

Ask a Pad-keeper what a continent was and they will tell you: a pad that had forgotten it was a pad.\
Fields ran to the horizon because the Soil Strand ran with them.\
Rivers kept to their beds because the Sprout Strand taught water manners.\
Cities did not float.
They hung, and hanging felt like standing, the way a well-tied hammock feels like a floor.
A maintained floor

The sky-floor was a job, not a miracle.\
Pad-keepers walked the hearths.\
Grit-singers listened for cracks.\
Rootbinders checked the living anchors.

Edge-walkers walked the rim and came back with a list.\
Drumhearts kept the beat so the rest of the work had a tempo.\
Pattern-weavers sang the factories that fed the rest.\
Colony-keepers kept the hives that kept the flowers that kept the roots.

Seal-carvers asked, politely, for exceptions.\
Loom-stitchers mended the roads so nobody had to jump.\
A continent that looked like ground was a continent whose last inspection had gone well.
Weather with a road

Rain did not guess. It followed Clock-sung channels along the lattice and arrived when the Pattern-weavers said it should. Storms were a Drumheart argument that got out of hand, then got walked back. Night was a veil the Seal-carvers asked for, politely, and the Loom kept the appointment.
You can still see the habit in the aurora. It is the sky trying to remember a schedule.
A schedule

Weather was a roster. You could set a table by it, because the table had been sung. Wind had a shift. Fog had a route. Harvest rain arrived on the day the Pattern-weavers marked, not when a cloud felt generous.
When the Cut came the appointments kept firing into empty air. That is why the aurora still tries. It is not pretty. It is a timetable with nobody on it.
Nine agreeing
No tribe could hold the sky alone. Soil without Stone is warmth with nowhere to stand. Spark without Clock is a beat with no song. Sigil without Spindle is a promise with no road home.
The old world was not peace. It was nine pulls kept taut at once. Peace was a side effect, and a thin one.
Maintenance

Nine tribes is nine jobs. They argued. They borrowed each other's tools and forgot to bring them back. They wrote rude notes on each other's drums. What they did not do was let a Strand slacken because they were sulking.
The floor held because the work got done in public. The Cut is what happens when maintenance stops: the hammock remembers it was never ground.
How the sky learns to hold
Nine agreements, kept in public.
How the sky holds

The sky does not snap back. It learns. A seated token is a lesson. Nine seated tokens are a pad that remembers how to be a floor. A Fragment seated is that pad telling the Dock it can stop holding its breath.
You are not restoring continents. You are teaching nine agreements to stay taut where everyone can see them.
Keep it public
A private mend is a secret. Secrets do not hold weather. The Tension Post hums for the whole Clowder. The Fray thins for the whole Dock. The lit thread, when it comes, is a server-wide fact.
Keep the work in the open. That is how the old sky held, and it is the only method the new one will accept.
What you are not

You will not get the hanging cities back. You will not get the schedule that let you set a table by the rain. You will get a sky that knows it is thread, and holds anyway.\
That is the better physics. Honest hammocks last longer than floors that lie.
Boots first
Then the bridge. Then the courage; it arrives on its own.
Boots first

The Edge-walkers kept footholds past the last fence post — cuts in the Loom that led somewhere on purpose. When the sky came apart they were already standing on the thin bits. Some of them walked people home. Some of them walked off the edge because that was the job.
Spiritgear was theirs: tools that spend Pulse instead of edge, so a foothold could be cut without wearing the mountain out.
What Claw mends

Seat Claw and fall damage stops within sight of the Post. That is a foothold, scaled to a pad. Edge is also when the braid opens: Pattern, Colony, Hum. The Edge-walkers never asked anyone to be brave in the same place twice. Pick a way and walk it.
The season the roots held
Roots are the only rope the void respects.
Roots held

The Rootbinders grew living anchors: March flora whose roots ran along the Strands and held pads that would otherwise have drifted. When the Loom was cut, those roots held for a season. Half of them. That season is why anything is still up here.
After that, the anchors went feral, or quiet, or into the March. You will meet what they became.
What Sprout mends

Food is infrastructure. A Clowder that eats well leaves the pad sooner because the Strand remembers being a continent's pantry. Seat Sprout and the Post feeds you a little. Plant something. The void respects a root more than a rope.
Where the fallen came to rest
A frayed-thread grave. A harbour. Halls sunk to the lintel.
March harbour

The March was always a road. After the Cut it became a harbour for whatever could still walk. Frayed thread washed up there the way wreckage finds a quiet bay. Camps. Halls. Drums that never learned how to quit. The March is a grave and a harbour at once. Treat it like both.
Halls to the lintel

Ancestor Halls stand in the steppe and highlands with their doors at the lintel — sunk, not fallen. Four tablets in each hall. Hollow Sentinels on a job nobody cancelled. Read every tablet. The dead are not asking for worship. They are asking for the record to be finished.
Where tension pools

In the crystal fields the remaining pull gathers: March Crystal, the Spire, the Loom-stitchers' waystation.\
Tension that had nowhere to seat ran downhill into stone that would hold it.\
That is why Reweave wants a March stone.\
You are not fetching a trophy.
You are bringing pooled tension home to a Post that can keep it.
Named by echo
Iron is low and patient. Diamond does not answer at all.
Named by echo
The Grit-singers named every shard by its voice. Iron is low and patient. Gold barely bothers to answer. Diamond does not answer at all; you find it by the silence around it.

When the Cut came, the meshes kept humming to nothing. Ore had nowhere to land. Continents that were mostly stone fell as gravel and still fall, somewhere below the void, if below still means anything.
What Stone mends

A mesh is not a finder. It is a welcome. Seat Stone and you are telling the ground it may arrive again. The Listening Pit, the Loomframe, the hammer chain — they are all the same courtesy: give the shard a place to sit.
Orphan engines
The drum is not loud. The drum is steady.
Orphan engines
The Drumhearts kept the beat under the whole sky. Spirit Pulse ran from their drums along the lattice to every tribe. When the Cut came, the drums did not stop. They had nobody left to stop for.
You will find engines still keeping time in the March and on pads that have not seen a cat in an age. Listen before you feed one. It may still be waiting for a beat you have not struck yet.
What Spark mends

Seat Spark and you are not inventing power. You are sitting down at a drum that never learned how to quit. Strike empty-handed, about a breath apart. The drum is not loud. The drum is steady. Be the drum.
Asked politely
Spirit goes where it is asked politely and stays where it is fed.
Asked politely

The Seal-carvers pressed spirit into matter and made it stay. A seal is a promise carved so the world has to keep it. A rite is asking the Loom, politely, for an exception. They cut blank seals by the thousand before the Cut, and asked for far too much.
Bind is their chapter. Braid Cord is spun at the Post once two peers are seated. That is not a recipe. That is three Strands agreeing in public.
What Sigil mends

Seat Sigil and you are allowed to ask again — smaller this time. Never bind what you would not be willing to unbind. Feed what you ask to stay. The old world broke on appetite. The new one will hold on manners.
Songs with no singer
Factories running. Drums beating. Gates open into nowhere.
Songs with no singer

After the Cut the world did not go quiet. It went unattended. Factories kept the round the Pattern-weavers had taught them. Drums kept the beat the Drumhearts had left in them. Gates stood open into nowhere because a Loom-stitcher had always meant to come back and close them after lunch.
Lunch did not come. The work did.
Asking politely

The Seal-carvers had a rule: spirit goes where it is asked politely and stays where it is fed. After the Cut, a lot of asking kept happening with nobody to feed the answer. Seals held promises to empty rooms. Rites fired into the Fray.
Polite is still the method. The budget is smaller. Ask for a pad, not a continent.
Asking too much

The old world broke on appetite as much as on slack. Exceptions stacked until the Loom had more appointments than thread. You will find blank seals by the thousand in the March. That is not treasure. That is a warning written in inventory.
Never bind what you would not unbind. Feed what you ask to stay. The new sky will hold on manners.
Songs still playing
A factory is a song that has stopped needing the singer.
Songs still playing

The Pattern-weavers sang factories the way you would sing a round: one figure, then the same figure again, until the work carried itself. When the Cut came the songs kept playing. Belts in empty halls. Clicks before a hum nobody owned.
Some are playing still. That is not haunting. That is good engineering with no audience.
What Clock mends

Seat Clock and you tell those songs they have a singer again. Create, timed plates, Song Thread — they are the same craft in different decades. A factory is a song that has stopped needing the singer. You are allowed to start it needing one.
Nine pulls, nine arguments
Maintenance stopped. Eight pulls became eight arguments. The Spindle seam tore.
Nine arguments

The Cut was not a war. It was the moment the work stopped being done. Nine tribes had nine pulls. When the schedule failed, eight of those pulls turned into eight arguments about whose fault the slack was. Blame is a kind of tension. It does not hold a sky.
The Spindle seam

The Loom-stitchers were the ones who mended the joins. While the others argued, the Spindle seam — the road between pads, the stitch that let nine pulls act as one floor — tore. Gates that should have led home led into weather. Weather that should have had a road had a hole.
A clock with no stitch is just nine ticking things, each sure it is on time.
What Clock knows

The Pattern-weavers kept trying to sing the factories through it. Songs do not stop because the choir is fighting. Seat Clock and you are not picking a side in the old argument. You are putting a tempo back under work that has been improvising since the Cut.
Roads into nowhere
They always meant to come back and mend them.
Roads into nowhere

The Loom-stitchers cut the gate-paths — into the March, into the Nether and End, into places the map does not have words for — and always meant to come back and mend them. They did not get to. Open gates dumped weather into the void. Closed ones trapped whole roads in the March, still walking.
What Spindle mends

Seat Spindle and you pick up a needle they dropped. The digital loom, the Gate Drum, a March stone, the Fragment. Nine seated, one stone, one right-click: the cut closes above your pad. They will not be there to thank you. Do it anyway.
What mending means
Nine agreeing, again.
Not the old world

Reweave does not put the continents back. It does not un-kill the guardians or un-scatter the tribes. It teaches nine Strands to hold a pad, then a Dock, then a sky that is honest about being made of thread.
The old world was a floor that pretended it was ground. The mended world is a floor that knows it is a promise.
A Clowder's share

When your Clowder seats the Fragment, your Strand of the Fray closes. Other Clowders still have theirs to do. You do not own the sky you just taught to hold. You own a share of the work, and the share is public.
A seated Fragment is a Clowder saying, in front of the Dock: we kept nine promises. The next Clowder still has nine to keep.
The Fray clock

The column over the Dock is not scenery.\
It is the only honest clock this campaign has.\
It thins when a Clowder reweaves.\
It turns to lit thread when every Clowder has done the same.

Go look at it.\
If it is still dark, the work is not finished — not because you failed, but because someone else has not had their hour yet.
Tablets and drums

The March kept the record.\
Ancestor Halls: four tablets each, three rooms, sentinels on a job nobody cancelled.\
Read every tablet before you call the work done.\
The Silent Drum in the highlands still takes four beats, a breath apart.

Strike it when you are ready.\
The Unsung is not a boss to loot.\
It is the March asking whether you learned the tempo.
Help them

If the Fray has gone to lit thread, the sky has learned to hold. If it has not, someone else still has work. Help them. Share a mesh. Walk their pad. Sit at their drum. Mending that stays on one Clowder's island is just a nicer hammock.
Tell the camps we are sorry it took so long. Then make sure it does not take that long for the next team.
book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.entry.t: Clowders
Teams, pads, and the Hall.
Clowders
A team is a **Clowder**. Clowders share a pad, share quests, and share Loom Tension: when one of you seats a Strand, all of you hear it.
Hall and Charter

**Goal:** claim a pad and reach the Hall.\
You need the **Island Charter** and a **Hub Key** (starter kit / Hall).\
1\. **K** or the **Island Charter** opens the island/team panel. Join or create a team, then pick a pad.\
2\. Right-click a friend with the Charter to invite, or `/clowder invite` / `/clowder accept`.

3\. Sneak-use the Charter on solid pad ground to seal spawn.\
4\. **Hub Key** or `/clowder hub` reaches Clowder Hall. `/clowder return` sends you home. Right-click a Hall Elder to trade Thread.\
**Check:** you are on the intended pad, and `/clowder hub` works.
Specialise

A Clowder does not have to climb everything in lockstep. Mid-campaign the braid opens three ways — Pattern, Colony, Hum — and any two carry the whole team into Bind.\
One of you can farm. One can drum. Nobody has to be everyone.
The Cut
Something severed the Loom.
The Cut
Something severed the Loom. The Codex does not know what. Neither did the tribes, by the end. One moment the sky was a floor. The next, the agreements failed in the same breath.
Continents fell. Weather forgot its roads. The tribes scattered with whatever dirt they could carry. What did not fall is what you are standing on: pads of earth the Strands still remember.
How it came apart

The Pad-keepers felt it first — hearths went cold while the sky still looked whole. Then the Rootbinders' living anchors held for a season, and that season is why anything is still up here. Guardians snapped in their arenas. Songs kept playing with nobody to hear them. Gate-paths stayed open into nowhere.
The Cut was not a war. It was a knot coming undone.
The Fray
Above the Dock stands a slow dark column. That is the cut itself — the **Fray** — standing over the place the sky used to knot.
It thins as Clowders tension Strands. When every Clowder has rewoven, it turns to lit thread. Go look at it now and then. It is the only clock this campaign has.
The Loom of Worlds
What held the sky up.
The Loom of Worlds

Before the void had a name, the sky was a floor.\
Nine Strands of living thread — Soil, Stone, Sprout, Claw, Spark, Clock, Swarm, Sigil, Spindle — were pulled taut by nine tribes of Ninjacats.\
Continents hung from that lattice the way fruit hangs from a well-kept vine.\
Weather ran along it.

Rain knew where to fall.\
Nothing dropped that was not meant to.
A sky that worked

Roads were not cut into dirt. They were sung into the thread and walked. Crops rooted into Strand as much as soil. Drums under one pad were heard as Pulse under another. The Loom was not a god and it was not a machine. It was nine agreements kept at once.
When the tribes pulled together, the horizon stayed put. That is the whole of the old physics.
What the tribes made

From their shared pull came **Tribal Power**: shamanic technomancy of Pulse, lattice, seal, and the road into the March-lands. Workshops that listen. Totems that speak in six voices. A drum that is not loud, only steady.\
The engines are still out there. Orphaned, humming, sacred. Treat them like an inheritance, not a scrap pile.
Skybound
You, on a pad, with a damaged book.
Skybound
You are Skybound: whoever the Loom dropped on a pad with enough grit to stay. The Codex teaches. Grave assigns the work. That is the arrangement.
Open **Grave** (backtick) for the assignment list. Click a quest item to open its recipe in JEI. This book is for why, and for how to place the work. They are the same campaign.
What fixing it means
You are not rebuilding the old continents. You are teaching nine Strands to agree again, one pad at a time. A seated token is a promise kept. A thinned Fray is the sky noticing.

When a Clowder reweaves, that Clowder's Strand of the sky closes. When every Clowder has done the same, the Fray turns to lit thread and stays that way. The world does not snap back. It learns to hold.
Nine Strands

Nine Strands still answer if pulled correctly: Soil, Stone, Sprout, Claw, Spark, Clock, Swarm, Sigil, Spindle.\
Each one ends in a **Strand token**. A token is proof, not fuel — it is never crafted, never consumed by a recipe. Seat it at a Tension Post and it stays seated.
Loom Tension
The Post, the seat, the hum.
Tension Post

**Goal:** raise a Post and seat the first token.\
You need logs, a **Binding Knot**, and a scrap of **Frayed Thread**.

Logs, a Binding Knot, and a scrap of Thread make a **Tension Post**. Raise one on the pad. Right-click it with a Strand token to seat that Strand; the notch lights, the tribe chimes, and the Post starts to hum.\
**Check:** the Soil notch is lit, and the pad starts mending you near the Post.
What Tension does
Seated Strands are **Loom Tension**. It is not a bar and it does not nag. It changes the pad.

Near the Post: the pad mends you (Soil). It feeds you a little (Sprout). Fall damage stops within sight of it (Claw). Hands quicken (five Strands). Luck (Sigil). And the horizon warms, one Strand at a time.
Spun at the Post

**Goal:** spin **Braid Cord**, then a **Spindle Loom Fragment**, at the Post — not the bench.\
You need **16 Strand Filaments**; **March Stone** once all nine are seated.\
**Braid Cord**: right-click holding **16 Strand Filaments**. No Strand has to be seated.

**Spindle Loom Fragment**: right-click with a March stone once all nine are seated. Seat the Fragment to Reweave.\
**Check:** 16 filaments at the Post give you Braid Cord, and a Fragment after nine seats plus March Stone.
Frayed Thread
Currency, string, and Hall stalls.
Frayed Thread

**Goal:** keep Thread as currency, and unravel it only when you need string.\
You need quest rewards, flint-mesh dirt on a Loomframe, or a steward cache.\
Every quest returns a little **Frayed Thread** — scraps of the Loom that still hold.

Unravel one for three string.\
Or keep it: **Kin stalls in Clowder Hall** (`/clowder hub`) sell saplings, buckets, meshes, pearls, and other things a pad runs short of.\
Right-click an Elder.\
**Check:** you can buy a sapling or mesh at a Hall Elder without going broke on string.
Earning Thread back

**Goal:** turn a mined stockpile into spendable Thread.\
You need blocks of copper, iron, gold, amethyst, emerald or diamond, or a netherite ingot.

**Grit** in Clowder Hall takes them across the counter for Thread. The rate is bad on purpose — a whole diamond block comes back as 24 Thread, and Spark sells two diamonds for 80 — so it is a way to spend a surplus, never a loop to farm. Stock returns each Minecraft day.
**Check:** you can price one life at the Spark stall (four Shards, 44 Thread Skeins each) and say how many blocks that is before you start digging.
Codex Pages

**Goal:** read a margin note without spending the page.\
You need a **Codex Page** from seating (every third Strand) or a Hall Kin stall.\
Every third Strand a Clowder seats, a **Codex Page** slips free — a margin note from that tribe. Right-click to read it. Pages are kept, not spent.

Hall Kin stalls at `/clowder hub` sell a few loose ones too. Those pick a tribe on their own.\
**Check:** right-click a page; it stays in your hand.
Voidloom
Yarn, knots, meshes, and two stations.
Void Yarn

**Goal:** have yarn without eating the whole string stock.\
You need four string (early) or string plus a pearl in the Tension Barrel.

Thread that remembers where it came from. Early: four string make two yarn. Later: string and an ender pearl in the Tension Barrel make two. The Loomframe combs a little out of dirt as **Loom Lint** — four lint, one yarn.
**Check:** JEI shows two yarn from four string, and you have yarn in the inventory.
Binding Knot

**Goal:** tie the Loom's soft gate so Recover stations can exist.\
You need Void Yarn and a slime ball (pad compost: dirt, seeds, bone meal).\
A ring of yarn around a slime ball. Early slime is pad compost: dirt, seeds, bone meal.

The Knot is the Loom's soft gate: Loomframes, Tension Posts, the first precision mechanism, and the AE2 controller all want one.\
**Check:** you hold a Binding Knot.
Loomframe

**Goal:** a hopper sieve that also catches Loom scraps.\
You need planks around a Binding Knot, a mesh, and grit.\
Stretch a mesh, load it with dirt, gravel, sand or dust, and let it work — one piece every few seconds with a shuttle clack.

Hoppers feed the top and pull from below.\
The mesh is hand-only.\
An oak sieve is still click; this machine is the hopper one.\
Thread meshes catch what Ex Deorum meshes do **and** the Loom's own scraps: Lint on string, Thread on flint, **Strand Filament** on iron (gravel, sand or dust).
**Check:** a hopper above feeds grit and a hopper below pulls scraps.
Tension Barrel

**Goal:** clay without a clay biome, and yarn from string plus a pearl.\
You need planks, string, Void Yarn, then water and dirt (or string and pearls).

Pour water (the bucket comes straight back), add up to eight dirt, come back for clay. String and pearls in the same barrel make yarn.\
Clay to porcelain clay to a porcelain bucket: that is how a pad first carries lava.
**Check:** empty-hand the barrel and take clay; the empty bucket came back when you poured.
The Nine Camps
Standing, offerings, marks.
Standing

Right-click a Tribe Hearth with what its tribe favours, or with a charged Pulse Cell, and your standing rises: Guest at 50, Friend at 150, Kin at 400, Voice at 800.\
Kills near the hearth, completed trades and finished requests count.
Hurting Kin costs 25 and turns the Hunters on you; breaking camp blocks costs five each, the hearth forty.
Tribe Mark

An Elder gives it at Voice, or for every third request you finish. With the tribe's Resonance Totem and two Spiritweave it becomes a Kinship Totem: an extra voice for the Pulse Resonator. Nine tribes can carry the song to fifteen voices.
Camp drum
A Drummer plays every few seconds. A Drumheart within eight blocks takes two Pulse from each beat, so a camp is a small, honest source of power. `/tribalpower standing` prints all nine standings.
Edge-walkers
Keepers of the Claw Strand.
Edge-walkers

The Edge-walkers kept footholds past the last fence post — cuts in the Loom that led somewhere on purpose. Spiritgear was theirs: tools that spend Pulse instead of edge.\
They left the footholds so nobody would have to be brave in the same place twice.

Before the Cut the rim was a job, not a dare: a list of places you could stand, a bridge already cut, courage allowed to arrive late.\
What they lost was a horizon that led somewhere on purpose.\
Some walked people home.\
Some walked off because that was the job.
The thin bits are still thin.
Claw Strand

*Boots first. Then the bridge. Then the courage; it arrives on its own.*\
Seated. The Edge-walkers answer when this Post hums.
Their camp
The Edge-walkers keep a camp in the March highlands: huts, a fire, a Tribe Hearth, a Fire totem, a banner and four Kin — an Elder, a Drummer, a Hunter and a Weaver.

Their hearth favours leather, iron, Rift Tooth. Their Elder talks: ask, and they trade Spiritgear and footholds, hand you the day's work, or tell the tribe's story. At Voice standing, or every third request you finish for them, they press the tribe's Mark into your hand.
Pattern-weavers
Keepers of the Clock Strand.
Pattern-weavers

The Pattern-weavers sang factories the way you would sing a round: one figure, then the same figure again, until the work carried itself.\
Their timed lattice songs are the ancestor of every belt and cog you will build. You already know this craft.

Before the Cut those songs fed hanging cities on a schedule you could set a table by. What they lost was the singer, not the song. Belts in empty halls. Clicks before a hum nobody owned. Seat Clock and you tell those songs they have a singer again.
Clock Strand

*A factory is a song that has stopped needing the singer.*\
Seated. The Pattern-weavers answer when this Post hums.
Their camp
The Pattern-weavers keep a camp in the March crystal fields: huts, a fire, a Tribe Hearth, a Air totem, a banner and four Kin — an Elder, a Drummer, a Hunter and a Weaver.

Their hearth favours redstone, clocks, Storm Wing. Their Elder talks: ask, and they trade timed songs and automation, hand you the day's work, or tell the tribe's story. At Voice standing, or every third request you finish for them, they press the tribe's Mark into your hand.
Elders that talk
Conversations, requests, stories, relics.
Elders that talk

Right-click a tribe's Elder and a conversation opens: what they say, and what you can say back. Trading is one thing you can ask for; work and their story are the others. A stranger gets a gruff word and a hint about the hearth. A Friend gets work. Finish their story and the welcome warms.
The camp's Drummer, Hunter and Weaver have a word for you too.
Requests

Ask an Elder for work and they hand you one of the tribe's requests: bring what they prize, deliver their dish cooked, turn back the dark's creatures near their fires, perform a rite in their camp, or raise a small build near it with Builder's Chalk in hand. The offers change with the days.

You may finish three requests a day across all the tribes; the Elder says so when the day's work is done. Each pays standing, and every third request you finish for one tribe pays a **Tribe Mark**, so you need not wait for Voice to hold one.
Nine stories

Ask an Elder to tell you their story and a seven-step road begins: become their Friend, bring the one thing they prize, hunt near their fires, sing a rite in their camp, cook their dish, and go where they send you. A step that asks for a rank you already hold moves straight on.
The last step is a **trial** against one of the March's own guardians. The Loom-stitchers' ends at The Unsung.
Nine relics

Finish a story and the Elder hands you the tribe's relic: Kept Ember, Ringing Stone, First Root, Bridge Nail, Steady Drum, Silent Gear, Hive Seal, Polite Seal, Ninth Thread.\
Carried anywhere in your pack, a relic keeps that tribe's boon on you whatever your standing.

All nine are the price of the Ninth Agreement.\
The Spirit Codex keeps score. Each tribe's page ends with their open request and where their story stands, and **Where to go next** opens with a **Next step** panel: one thing to do, from the first hearth to the Ninth Agreement, moving as you go.
The living March
Weather, surges, festivals, spirits, the Chronicle.
March weather

The March acts on its own now.\
The Spirit Codex's **The living March** page shows what it is doing: the weather, the surge, whose festival it is.\
A storm or a surge is called two minutes before it sets in, in chat and on the action bar.

That is your time to find a roof or step off a crossing.\
Four countries have weather beyond rain, and spirits rise under it by day as they would at night.\
**Ashfall** over the Ember Wastes feeds Ember Horns and chokes Wind Harps.

A **Glimmer Storm** over the Crystal Fields feeds Wake Bells and dulls Drumhearts.\
A **Whiteout** on the Snow Fields drives Wind Harps and freezes Wave Drums.\
**Fen Mist** in the Reed Fen swells Wave Drums and damps Ember Horns.\
Weather comes and goes whether or not anyone is there to see it.
Ley surges
Now and then one voice's ley threads run bright. Through the Ley Lens they blaze and the lens names the voice; every Ley Collector whose threads carry it yields double while the surge lasts.

Stand on a bare crossing — where a cell's threads meet, with no collector to drink it — and the surge gives you **Ley Sickness**: the ground sways and your Pulse drains.\
Step off it.\
A remedy, the Healing Circle or a night at the Sweat Stones lifts it.
Festivals, spirits

Every tribe keeps a festival day, the nine taking turns.\
On their day the camp's fires burn, the hearth throws its colour into the air and the Kin keep to it.
The Elder has festival words and a gift for anyone who joins the feast; a rite performed in the camp that day earns festival thanks, and a feast eaten by the hearth counts you at their table.
Rarely a warm light drifts near you out in the March. It does not flee. Reach it and it tells you a line of its country's story, leaves a small gift, and goes.
The Chronicle

Sixteen fragments of the Loom's history are carved into the March: eight **Carved Stones** in the walls of its ruins, from the Loom Ruin and the Stilt Village to the Ossuary and the Glimmer Vault, and eight two-by-two **Murals** at the guardians' grounds.

Right-click one and you read it; the Spirit Codex keeps it under **The Chronicle**, in order.\
Read all sixteen and the story is whole.\
Both can be picked up and set on a wall of your own. A mural is placed as one piece and comes down as one.
Guardians of the March
Eight altars, eight cores, one agreement.
March guardians

Not the Snapped Guardians of the arenas: these are the March's own, one per country, each the end of a tribe's story.\
The **Slag Titan** in the Ember Wastes.\
The **Bog Matriarch** in the Reed Fen.\
The **Cairn Wight** on the Snow Fields.

The **Prism Serpent** in the Crystal Fields.\
The **Vault Sentinel** on Glimmer Ridge.\
The **Tide Drummer** in the Shallows.\
The **Stampede Spirit** on the Steppe.

The **Storm Roc** on the Highlands.\
The ninth trial is The Unsung, at the Drum Circle.
Guardian grounds

Each country has a ring of its own stone with a **Guardian Altar** at its centre.\
A guardian rises only from its altar: on polished deepslate, between four lit candles, with open sky above, and it rests twenty minutes between calls.

Sneak-use the altar with an empty hand and it tells you what it wants: a fistful of that country's reagent.\
JEI's **Guardian calls** page lists them.\
Warded ground refuses the call and keeps your reagents.
Two phases

Every guardian has a signature attack — slams, snares, frost breath, light bolts, sweeps, tides, charges, swoops — that sharpens at half health, when it also calls its country's creatures to its side.\
Those drop nothing and vanish when it falls.

Leave it alone half a minute and it goes back to sleep and frees its altar.\
It is a boss in every sense: a boss bar in its tribe's colour, no knockback, no potions, no leash, no Soul Urn, no bed while one stands.

When it falls, everyone who fought finishes that tribe's trial, and it drops its **core** with a heap of its country's reagents. A core and a Loom Thread make six Resonant Cores; keep one of each of the eight for what comes next.
The Ninth Agreement

The eight cores — Slag Core, Fen Heart, Cairn Stone, Prism Core, Vault Seal, Tide Shell, Herd Horn, Storm Plume — and an Unsung Heart make the tablet.\
Draw a Loom circle and perform the rite with all nine relics on you.

Nine lights rise, one in each tribe's colour, and the Loom agrees again.\
After: every tribe treats you as Kin at the least, all nine boons settle on you for a while, and the March's aurora burns full and steady every night you stand under it. The world remembers it for good.
Reweave
The cut, closed.
Reweave

Nine tribes, one thread. Your Clowder closed its Strand of the sky.\
The Fray over the Dock is thinner for it. When every Clowder has done the same, it turns to lit thread and stays that way.\
Go and see what the March kept for you. Tell it we are sorry it took so long.
Seal-carvers
Keepers of the Sigil Strand.
Seal-carvers

The Seal-carvers pressed spirit into matter and made it stay. A seal is a promise carved so the world has to keep it; a rite is asking the Loom, politely, for an exception.\
Never bind what you would not be willing to unbind.

Before the Cut they carved promises by the thousand — exceptions asked politely, then asked again, then asked too much. What they lost was manners with a budget. Bind is their chapter. The old world broke on appetite. The new one will hold on asking smaller.
Sigil Strand

*Spirit goes where it is asked politely and stays where it is fed.*\
Seated. The Seal-carvers answer when this Post hums.
Their camp
The Seal-carvers keep a camp in the March highlands: huts, a fire, a Tribe Hearth, a Spirit totem, a banner and four Kin — an Elder, a Drummer, a Hunter and a Weaver.

Their hearth favours blank and element seals, Spirit Shards. Their Elder talks: ask, and they trade the tribe's Seal, Blank Seals and rite tablets, hand you the day's work, or tell the tribe's story. At Voice standing, or every third request you finish for them, they press the tribe's Mark into your hand.
Pad-keepers
Keepers of the Soil Strand.
Pad-keepers

The Pad-keepers kept the hearths. Not the fires — the *warmth*: the banked heat in thin dirt that let a pad hold a family through a long dark.\
They were the first to notice the Loom was fraying, because the pads got cold before anything fell.

Before the Cut they banked heat under whole continents: hearths under markets, under fields, under the first stair of every hanging city. What they lost was the long dark they had already solved — warmth as a public fact. Now they keep scraps, and they keep them anyway.
Soil Strand

*We never called it dirt. We called it what was left, and we kept it warm.*\
Seated. The Pad-keepers answer when this Post hums.
Their camp
The Pad-keepers keep a camp in the March steppe: huts, a fire, a Tribe Hearth, a Earth totem, a banner and four Kin — an Elder, a Drummer, a Hunter and a Weaver.

Their hearth favours dirt and moss blocks, bread, Echo Shards. Their Elder talks: ask, and they trade hearths and caches, hand you the day's work, or tell the tribe's story. At Voice standing, or every third request you finish for them, they press the tribe's Mark into your hand.
Drumhearts
Keepers of the Spark Strand.
Drumhearts

The Drumhearts kept the beat under the whole sky. Spirit Pulse — power as rhythm before it was a number — ran from their drums along the lattice to every tribe.\
The orphan engines you find still keep their time. Listen before you feed one.

Before the Cut the beat was civic: Pulse as a utility, drums as the sky's metronome, every pad on the same downbeat.\
What they lost was an audience.\
The engines did not stop.\
They had nobody left to stop for.
You will find them still keeping time, waiting for a beat you have not struck yet.
Spark Strand

*The drum is not loud. The drum is steady. Be the drum.*\

Loom-stitchers

The Loom-stitchers cut the gate-paths — into the March, into the Nether and End, into places the map does not have words for — and always meant to come back and mend them.\
They did not get to. You will.

Before the Cut they kept the roads between pads, between worlds, between the March and home. What they lost was the appointment. Open gates dumped weather into the void. Closed ones trapped whole roads still walking. The Spindle seam tore while the other eight pulls turned into arguments. You pick up the needle they dropped.
Spindle Strand

*The Loom was never one thread. It was nine agreeing.*\
Seated. The Loom-stitchers answer when this Post hums.
Their camp
